publications.title: Redefining Research Crowdsourcing: Incorporating Human Feedback with LLM-Powered Digital Twins
publications.subtitle: CHI EA '25 LBW
publications.description: Crowd work platforms like Amazon Mechanical Turk and Prolific are vital for research, yet workers’ growing use of generative AI tools poses challenges. Researchers face compromised data validity as AI responses replace authentic human behavior, while workers risk diminished roles as AI automates tasks. To address this, we propose a hybrid framework using digital twins, personalized AI models that emulate workers’ behaviors and preferences while keeping humans in the loop. We evaluate our system with an experiment (n=88 crowd workers) and in-depth interviews with crowd workers (n=5) and social science researchers (n=4). Our results suggest that digital twins may enhance productivity and reduce decision fatigue while maintaining response quality. Both researchers and workers emphasized the importance of transparency, ethical data use, and worker agency. By automating repetitive tasks and preserving human engagement for nuanced ones, digital twins may help balance scalability with authenticity.

publications.title: FairFare: A Tool for Crowdsourcing Rideshare Data to Empower Labor Organizers
publications.subtitle: arXiv
publications.description: Rideshare workers experience unpredictable working conditions due to gig work platforms' reliance on opaque AI and algorithmic systems. In response to these challenges, we found that labor organizers want data to help them advocate for legislation to increase the transparency and accountability of these platforms. To address this need, we collaborated with a Colorado-based rideshare union to develop FairFare, a tool that crowdsources and analyzes workers' data to estimate the take rate -- the percentage of the rider price retained by the rideshare platform. We deployed FairFare with our partner organization that collaborated with us in collecting data on 76,000+ trips from 45 drivers over 18 months. During evaluation interviews, organizers reported that FairFare helped influence the bill language and passage of Colorado Senate Bill 24-75, calling for greater transparency and data disclosure of platform operations, and create a national narrative. Finally, we reflect on complexities of translating quantitative data into policy outcomes, nature of community based audits, and design implications for future transparency tools.

projects.title: Herbal Decode
projects.description: At Herbal Decode, we are building a nonprofit initiative that merges Traditional & Complementary Medicine (TCM) with cutting-edge machine learning to accelerate drug discovery and expand global access to affordable, herbal-based healthcare. As co-founders, we lead efforts in strategic planning, AI model development, cross-border collaboration, and scientific outreach.Our mission is to decode centuries of herbal wisdom using modern technology, validate it through clinical data, and create scalable, science-backed solutions for the future of healthcare. We will be working closely with Princeton-affiliated researchers, TCM experts, hospitals, and global institutions to build the world's first comprehensive AI model for traditional medicine.Focused on impact, innovation, and accessibility—we're redefining how the world understands and uses natural medicine.

projects.title: Princeton Independent Work #2 | Spring 2025
projects.description: Decoding the Language of Resistance: LGBTQ+ Coded Language on Weibo in the Context of Censorship and Community BuildingThis project explores the emergence and circulation of LGBTQ+ coded language on Weibo inresponse to Chinese state censorship, using a dataset of over 850K posts from 2010 to 2025.Through lead-lag temporal analysis, frequency tracking, and OCR of image-based content, ittraces how euphemisms, neologisms, and visual strategies are used both to evade detection andto build queer community. Findings show that coded terms often arise within tightly networkedqueer groups before diffusing outward, with usage spikes linked to political events or momentsof queer visibility. Drawing on Sara Ahmed’s affective orientation, Martin Manalansan’s queerworlding, and Kathleen Stewart’s weak theory, this study argues that queer-coded language onWeibo is not only a form of resistance but a practice of affective and semiotic world-making,contributing to broader discussions in digital humanities, queer theory, linguistic anthropology,and censorship studies.

projects.title: Princeton Independent Work #1 | Fall 2024
projects.description: Driving Insights: User-Centered Design Research for Enhancing the Driver’sSeat AppThe gig economy has grown rapidly, offering flexibility to workers through platforms like Uber,Lyft, and DoorDash. However, gig drivers face significant challenges, including financialinstability, logistical inefficiencies, and safety concerns, which are often exacerbated by limitedaccess to user-friendly tools tailored to their needs. In collaboration with the Princeton HCI Lab, this study investigates the pain points of gigdrivers and proposes actionable recommendations for redesigning the Driver’s Seat app, a toolaimed at improving their workflows and earnings transparency. Using a user-centered approach,11 semi-structured interviews were conducted with gig drivers, both users and non-users of theapp. Thematic coding of the qualitative data revealed key issues, such as the need for real-timesafety alerts, automated deadhead mile tracking, and a centralized dashboard for multi-appintegration. Based on these findings, this paper outlines a prioritized set of features for the appredesign and evaluates their potential impact on usability and user satisfaction. While resourceconstraints limited the immediate scope of implementation, additional features such asevent-based demand forecasting and airport activity integration are proposed for futuredevelopment. By addressing the unique challenges faced by gig drivers, this research contributesto creating a more effective and user-centered solution within the gig economy.

projects.title: TimeTrace
projects.description: TimeTrace is a better Chrome history that not only allows you to see how much time you’ve spent exactly on each website and find websites in a jiff, but it also categorizes each website for you and breaks down your browser activity for you to help you become a better browser user.Features include:- A scaled, continuous timeline that shows all browser activity and time spent on each website.- A powerful search bar that comes with fuzzy search, allowing users to search the content of any website they've ever browsed.Upcoming features:- Smart timeline summary- AI Co-pilot- OCR on screenshots and PDF searchIn the future, TimeTrace will go off-browser and become your personal life co-pilot that specializes in information recall by building your own personal databases while leveraging AI-augmented information retrieval to help you retrieve and categorize information from emails, texts, online drives, productivity and note-taking apps, and everything else digital.
